closure_challenge.name: Closure-challenge benchmark
closure_challenge.our_entry: Entry of record (round 5, 2026-08-07) scored 0.0566 overall through the benchmark's own unmodified harness across six pre-registered scoring calls (RANS-identity floor, round-1 periodic-hills correction, round-2 extended to ducts and NASA hump, round-3 test-blind decline-gate, round-4 Reynolds-invariant duct rescale, round-5 untrained QCR2000 forward solve on the ducts). Rank 1 of 5 scored locally at benchmark commit deb91557 - a local scoring, not an official placement. P(rank 1) = 68%: a case-level bootstrap over the eight scored cases puts the probability that this ordering survives a comparable set of cases at 68%, and an eight-case sample cannot pin that tighter than 2-100% at 95%. Best result on the public board on four of the eight test cases - but two of those four (alpha_05_4071_4048, alpha_05_4071_2024) are the organisers' own unmodified RANS field, which our decline gate passed through untouched; the credit there belongs to the baseline every entrant is handed for free, not to our model, and anyone submitting it unchanged scores exactly the same. Not yet submitted to the benchmark's steward. The lead is not statistically decided: the 0.002878 margin over Reissmann sits against a per-case spread five times larger, so on a different set of eight cases the ordering could reverse, and the same is true of the margin over Wu and Zhang; the margins over Liu and Montoya do survive that test. The standing is two cases wide - on the eight-case mean, alpha_15_13929_2024 alone supplies more than the whole margin and NASA_2DWMH alone costs more than it. AR_1_Ret_360 and AR_3_Ret_360 are ties below the precision the board publishes to, and are not per-case wins.
